name: Port Light
description: Scotch, lemon, and orgeat—a tiki sour that uses the whiskey already on the shelf.
history: A mid-century tiki sour, usually credited to Don the Beachcomber’s later menus and then to Trader Vic’s. Scotch stands in for rum; orgeat is the sweetener.
whyItWorks: Orgeat softens Scotch smoke the way it softens rum; lemon keeps the drink a sour instead of a dessert.
steps: Shake Scotch, lemon, and orgeat hard with ice.
Fine-strain into a chilled coupe, or dump over crushed ice.
techniqueNotes: Macallan 12 is polite here; a peatier Scotch will read as smoke and almond.
